title: A multicentre PROspective study on the diagnostic value of Steroid profiling in primary ALDOsteronism: The PROSALDO study
summary:
The PROSALDO Studie is a diagnostic study which tests a new blood assay for its usefulness in the diagnosis of primary aldosteronism. Primary aldosteronism is a disease which is caused by too much aldosterone secreted from one or both adrenal glands. Patients with this disease suffer from severe blood pressure. Currently, it is difficult to diagnose primary aldosteronism. The new test could simplify the diagnostic approach. 

Main objective: to answer the question whether a baseline blood test (several Steroids measured from one sample) is superior in diagnostic terms in predicting the presence or absence of the most frequent form of hormone induced hypertension, primary aldosteronism.

Background of study: Endocrine hypertension, such as overactivity of adrenal gland hormone secretion (primary aldosteronism), is very frequent affecting up to 10% of all hypertenisves. Currently, the diagnostic steps to verify the presence of primary aldosteronism is cumbersome.

Patients to be included: hypertensive patients with one or more features of the following:
-difficult to control blood pressure (3 or more drugs)
-blood presssure >150/100
-spontanous hypokalemia
-severe blood pressur at young age or a Family history of hypertension

interventions.name: Steroid Profile measured with LCMS to diagnose primary aldosteronismus

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Male and female adult patients (18-70 yr) with hypertension who are suspected to have PA and in whom other causes of secondary hypertension have been excluded according to standard clinical criteria
• All subjects must have read, understood and signed the informed consent  form before inclusion into the study protocol
Exclusion criteria:
• Patients with other forms of secondary hypertension
• Subjects who need medications that may interfere with or invalidate outcome parameters (e.g., steroids, oral contraceptives)
• Patients with low or low-normal aldosterone (basal aldosterone <6.1 ng/dl) (<170 pmol/l)
• Pregnancy 
• Patients with impaired mental capacity that precludes informed consent
• Patients at risk of allergic reaction to contrast media
• Unsuitability for or objection to undergo AVS, CT or adrenal surgery
• Severe or terminal co-morbidity which seriously interferes with possible treatment or health related quality of life
